Netflix Business Insights Report

Executive report · Data Analysis Using Python Internship · Auspify Technologies

By BENIMANA Theophile · BenTech Rwanda

Summary1. EDA2. Trends 3. Dashboards4. Insights 5. Next stepsMethod

Executive Summary

This report studies the Netflix catalogue of 8,786 unique titles to find what the platform offers, how it is changing, and what the business can do next.

8,786
Unique titles
6,123
Movies
2,663
TV Shows
86
Countries
42
Genres
63%
Not led by USA

Top findings

  • Catalogue growth over time. Most titles were added in 2019 (2,013). The latest year in the data, 2021, has 1,498 (74% of the peak; it may be a partial year).
  • Movies and TV shows: how the mix moves. Movies are 70% of the catalogue. The TV show share of new additions went from 32% in 2015 to 34% in 2021.
  • Share of international content. 63% of titles are not led by the USA. This share moved from 38% in 2015 to 63% in 2021. India is the biggest non-US country with 1,056 titles.

Step 2 - Key Trends and Patterns

  • Most titles were added in 2019.
  • The TV show share of new additions moved from 32% to 34%.
  • 63% of titles are not led by the USA.
  • The busiest month for additions is July.
  • The top genre is International Movies.

Step 4 - Business Insights

Content Strategy

1. Catalogue growth over time

What we found: Most titles were added in 2019 (2,013). The latest year in the data, 2021, has 1,498 (74% of the peak; it may be a partial year).

What to do: Check first whether the drop is real or only an incomplete year. If it is real, focus the budget on fewer, higher-quality titles instead of adding volume.

Content Strategy

2. Movies and TV shows: how the mix moves

What we found: Movies are 70% of the catalogue. The TV show share of new additions went from 32% in 2015 to 34% in 2021.

What to do: TV shows are taking a bigger share of new titles. Series usually keep subscribers coming back every week, so keep investing in them, especially returning series.

Global Expansion

3. Share of international content

What we found: 63% of titles are not led by the USA. This share moved from 38% in 2015 to 63% in 2021. India is the biggest non-US country with 1,056 titles.

What to do: Keep investing in local stories from the top non-US countries, starting with India. Local titles can also be promoted to viewers in other countries.

Audience

4. Audience mix of the catalogue

What we found: Adults is the biggest group with 46% of titles. Kids is the smallest with 10%.

What to do: Look at the Kids group first. It has the fewest titles, so adding more could reach viewers the catalogue serves less today. Check viewing data before investing.

Programming

5. How concentrated the genres are

What we found: The top 3 genres (International Movies, Dramas, Comedies) make up 36% of all genre tags. The biggest is 'International Movies' with 2,751 titles.

What to do: Keep the strong genres, and test smaller genres that match what viewers in growing countries ask for, so the catalogue does not depend on only a few genres.

Content Strategy

6. Age of titles when they are added

What we found: A title was on average 1.3 years old when added in 2015 and 5.8 years old in 2021.

What to do: Netflix adds older titles more often now. Licensed older content is cheap filler, so balance it with new originals to keep the catalogue feeling fresh.

Release Planning

7. Additions follow a monthly pattern

What we found: July is the busiest month (827 titles) and February is the quietest (562).

What to do: Plan big releases for February and other quiet months, so viewers have something new all year and big titles do not compete with each other.

Programming

8. Movie length and show format

What we found: The middle movie runs 98 minutes and 19% of movies are longer than 2 hours. 67% of TV shows have only one season.

What to do: Many shows stop after one season. Look at why, since renewing the successful ones is cheaper than starting new shows.

Data Quality

9. Missing information in the raw data

What we found: 0% of titles have no director and 0% have no country in the original file.

What to do: Make director and country required when titles are added. Better data gives better search, recommendations and reports.

Step 5 - Recommended Next Steps

  1. Content Strategy: Check first whether the drop is real or only an incomplete year. If it is real, focus the budget on fewer, higher-quality titles instead of adding volume.
  2. Content Strategy: TV shows are taking a bigger share of new titles. Series usually keep subscribers coming back every week, so keep investing in them, especially returning series.
  3. Global Expansion: Keep investing in local stories from the top non-US countries, starting with India. Local titles can also be promoted to viewers in other countries.
  4. Audience: Look at the Kids group first. It has the fewest titles, so adding more could reach viewers the catalogue serves less today. Check viewing data before investing.
  5. Programming: Keep the strong genres, and test smaller genres that match what viewers in growing countries ask for, so the catalogue does not depend on only a few genres.
  6. Content Strategy: Netflix adds older titles more often now. Licensed older content is cheap filler, so balance it with new originals to keep the catalogue feeling fresh.
  7. Release Planning: Plan big releases for February and other quiet months, so viewers have something new all year and big titles do not compete with each other.
  8. Programming: Many shows stop after one season. Look at why, since renewing the successful ones is cheaper than starting new shows.
  9. Data Quality: Make director and country required when titles are added. Better data gives better search, recommendations and reports.

Method and Limits

  • Data was cleaned in Task 1: duplicates removed, missing values filled, text standardized.
  • A title with several countries or genres is counted once for each of them.
  • The data describes the catalogue, not viewing hours, so the findings show what is offered, not what is most watched.
  • The latest year may be incomplete. The findings show patterns and are not proof of cause.
